items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: he and I became great friends within a few days after I joined Kirk.

ctx.x: I had heard about Dick Wilson being a great tenor player before I joined the band and he was considered on a par with Hershel Evans. To me, his tone was not as heavy as Hershel's, but his ideas were great and he was a hard swinger. Dick was a very heavy drinker, I soon found out, because he and I became great friends within a few days after I joined Kirk. Big Jim would drink and eat, and so did I. But Dick ate almost nothing and his drinking did not show in his playing.

There was a liquor store near the theatre that gave credit to the people working at the theatre and there was also a joint across the street from the stage entrance that sold juice and stayed open all night. I hung out with Dick in this place after our last shows unitl I could not keep my eyes open and would leave him there almost every morning. I lived at a boarding house just in front of the theatre. When we closed at the Howard, I had a liquor bill of forty-five dollars and the salary for the week was eighty…
